messages:
IncidentBot: :rotating_light: ALERT — Multiple 5xx spikes from us-west-2 regional edge (ingest, routing). Auto failover attempted and partially applied; traffic-shift reported 50% success, but many connections are timing out. Pager sent to oncall@redwood.

oncall-bot: paging alex chen (primary oncall) and maya singh (backup). Severity: P1.

alex chen: I’m on it. Looking at dashboard — spikes started ~2m ago, RTTs to some AZs in us-west-2 show packet loss >40%.

maya singh: I see healthcheck flaps on the NLBs in us-west-2 (target group reports 85% unhealthy). Route53 failover policy tried to move some traffic to us-east-1 but TTLs and cached connections kept old connections hitting broken AZ.

jia wu: Are we seeing BGP route withdrawals or cloud provider network issues? Any Provider status?

luke morris: AWS shows partial network degradation in us-west-2a per their status page. They’ve marked a subset of AZ networking as degraded. This is consistent with packets being blackholed.

alex chen: Confirmed: control plane attempted canary shift to us-east-1 via traffic-shift job #3245. It reported success but the edge gateways in us-west kept forwarding for existing sessions. Need immediate mitigation to reduce customer impact.

ops-bot: current customer impact estimate: ~18% of requests from west coast receive 503/504. Top affected customers via quota: 3 enterprise tenants showing elevated error rates.

maya singh: Plan: 1) pause auto-scaling in us-west to stop unstable drain churn 2) create forced route53 weighted update to move 90% traffic to us-east-1 3) set low TTL to expedite propagation 4) coordinate with infra to tombstone unhealthy NLBs. Agree?

alex chen: Yes. I’ll do the route53 step, but we should not lower TTL too low if it can increase DNS query volume. Set to 60s for immediate mitigation.

jia wu: While DNS propagates, we should also push a config to edge proxies to prefer us-east endpoints for new sessions. That will help clients honoring keep-alives to new connections. Rolling that now.

alex chen: Route53 weighted record change executed: 
```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z2ABCDEF --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"route-east","Weight":90,"TTL":60,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"52.23.12.34"}]}}]}'
```

ops-bot: change propagated to nameservers; expected effect within TTL windows.

maya singh: Edge proxy preference applied: updated proxy upstream map to bias us-east by 90% for region=us-west client IPs. Config snippet: 
```
upstreams: prefer-east: weight=9/1
```
Rolling to edges now (50% batch).

luke morris: Infra confirm: we’re seeing connection resets from us-west-2a+2b. We will mark NLB target group tgr-89 as draining and remove instances in the affected AZs to avoid returning them to healthy state prematurely.

alex chen: Executing target group drain: 
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:targetgroup/tgr-89 --targets Id=i-0abcde12345
```

support-bot: Logged customer impact notice for enterprise tenants: "We are currently mitigating a regional network issue affecting a portion of us-west-2 traffic. Failover in progress; reduced error rates expected as traffic moves to us-east-1. Updates every 15m."

jia wu: Quick healthcheck: synthetic canary to us-east-1 shows 200s in <200ms. West coast canary still 503 in affected AZs. Traffic shift visible in backend metrics: requests in us-east increased ~4x.

maya singh: Important: We observed an unexpected behavior where our traffic-shift job left some session-affine routes pinned at the edge (TCP keep-alive). We should proactively close long-lived connections on edge gateways in the affected POPs to force reconnection. Initiating graceful conn close.

luke morris: Executed graceful close on edge-gateways west-pop-11 and west-pop-12. Commands: 
```
ssh edge@west-pop-11 -- sudo systemctl restart edge-proxy
# or: edgectl drain-sessions --pop west-pop-11 --grace 10s
```

alex chen: After DNS update + proxy bias + draining, error rate dropped from 18% to ~4% within 10m. Customer-facing telemetry matches support-bot notice.

ops-bot: Current customer impact estimate: reduced to 4%. Still a handful of enterprise customers with elevated error rates due to DNS cache stubbornness or ISP caching.

maya singh: We need to prepare for longer tail: increase capacity in us-east by spinning an extra worker pool to handle burst. I’m kicking off a scale-up job (dedicated pool + reserved capacity override).

jia wu: Also filing a post-incident action: check our traffic-shift logic for session-affinity handling and improve edge preference/TTL coordination. Ticket created: INC-2026-447.

alex chen: Handoff: I’m going offline in 20m. Maya, take primary until fully stabilized. Leave notes: route53 weighted record at 90% east, TTL=60, proxies biased, NLB targets in us-west draining, infra investigating AZ-level network flaps.

maya singh: Acknowledged — I’m primary. I’ll keep watch and update every 15m. If error rate creeps >8% re-escalate to SRE lead.

luke morris: AWS says they’ve routed additional capacity around the affected devices but are still probing root cause. They expect intermittent recovery in the next 30–60 minutes for some AZs.

support-bot: Notified affected customers with an updated ETA: "Mitigation applied; continued monitoring. Next update 30m or when status changes."

maya singh: Current status summary for postmortem: cause: AWS AZ-level network degradation causing packet loss and unhealthy NLB targets; primary mitigation: manual DNS weighted shift + edge proxy bias + forced draining of unhealthy targets; customer impact: ~18% error rates peak, 20 minutes heavy impact window, residual tail to 4% over next 30m. Action items: improve session-affinity handling in traffic-shift, automate edge conn-close during failover, review TTL defaults for failover records.

alex chen: thanks all — handing off completely now.

oncall-bot: Handoff recorded: alex chen -> maya singh at 1723503200.

maya singh: I'll coordinate the post-incident writeup once AWS confirms root-cause. Marking incident as still open but mitigation in place.

luke morris: Noted. I’ll attach NLB health logs + BGP/route tracing for the postmortem.

IncidentBot: Incident P1 (1723500123) mitigation in progress. Updates will be posted in this thread. :white_check_mark:
